bestiary.codenamecoraline.title: Bestiary
bestiary.codenamecoraline.intro: A traveller's notes on the creatures folklore left in the ruins: the mystic side, how they attack and where to find them. Every new creature gets a chapter.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.name: Redcap
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.cover.c: Fig. 1: a spear Redcap, in profile.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.folklor: Also called Powrie or Dunter, the Redcap belongs to the Unseelie Court: the sinister caste of the fairy folk of the Scottish borders. It plays no pranks: it kills whoever crosses its path, unprovoked. They say it is born where there was massacre and tyranny, and that every bloody ruin breeds its own.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.blood.b: The cap is the heart of the creature. The tales swear its cloth must be dyed with fresh blood, or the goblin withers. So it never flees a fight and never leaves a traveller in peace. And it wears iron boots, the metal that harms the fair folk: a blasphemy that makes it even more feared.
They strike from very close, in quick successive cuts. No reach: beyond a block and a half you are safe.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.claws.b: Unarmed, they scratch up close. From afar they hurl pebbles: between 5 and 16 blocks. They anticipate your step.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.attacks: SPEAR: a long, slow thrust of about two blocks. Sidestep it and get inside its reach. DAGGER: quick cuts up close; back off between blows. CLAWS: scratch up close and aim the pebble where you will be: change direction, never run in a straight line.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.pack.bo: When one picks a victim it laughs, and the others take the same target. Spear and dagger Redcaps surround, take opposite sides and charge together. The claws stay behind, lobbing pebbles. Hurting one wakes them all. Fight in a corridor, back to the wall.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.cap.bod: Whoever wears the cap is taken for one of their own: they do not attack and they help against whoever hurts the wearer. Take it off in their sight and the pack's fury lasts half a minute.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.where.b: Ruins of old blood: strongholds, ruined portals, trail ruins, ancient cities and abandoned pillager towers, preferably at night, and almost always one to a place. (Traveller's note: I never saw one born on its own; for now it is only summoned with the egg.)
bestiary.codenamecoraline.redcap.drops.b: Nail and tooth: common, useful to those who know potions. Rusted weapons: rare, worn at random, from nearly new to nearly broken; only the one that carried a weapon drops it. The cap: very rare, and the most valuable of all. Only taken from one you kill with your own hands.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.name: Basilisk
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.anato: A low, fin-tailed amphibian bearing two huge golden growths. These false eyes never blink. Its real eyes are tiny points beside the snout. Its throat swells before it exhales. Inspired by the Basilisks of Elden Ring.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.habit: Hostile and common. Groups of four to eight appear in swamps and mangroves, even during the day. They also inhabit caves throughout the Overworld: beneath the terrain, with no visible sky and light seven or lower. They need solid ground and never spawn in Peaceful. They leap at travellers within ten blocks.
Listen for the inhale: you have 1.2 seconds to move. The mist lasts five seconds within 3.5 blocks of its centre. It applies Blindness and Wither III for five seconds: hearts turn black and health drains rapidly. Solid walls block exposure.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.survi: Leave the mist. Wither III can kill; milk removes both effects. The potion brewed from a Basilisk leg, eye and tail protects against both for three minutes. Fire deals 50% extra damage; swords deal 25% extra. Poison, Wither and Darkness cannot harm the creature.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.light: Hold a soul torch or soul lantern in either hand. The Basilisk stops attacking and retreats about six blocks. Strike it yourself and it remembers you: your soul flame will no longer repel that individual. Existing mist remains dangerous.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.basilisk.spoil: On death, a Basilisk may drop one leg (50%), one eye (25%) and one tail (35%). Rolls are independent, in any biome. All three parts are used, in that order, at a brewing stand to prepare Wither and Blindness Resistance.
Fuel the stand with blaze powder. Brew water with nether wart, then leg, eye and tail in order. Each step takes twenty seconds for up to three bottles. Cures and blocks Wither and Blindness for three minutes; redstone extends to eight. Gunpowder: splash. Dragon breath: lingering. Milk removes protection.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.ana: The Lithophage (Litófago) is an ancient subterranean creature formed of hardened clay and minerals. It remains motionless for long periods and awakens when it detects a threat in its territory.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.hab: Inhabits Lush Caves primarily and Dripstone Caves secondarily, between Y = -20 and Y = 20. Spawns in dark chambers in groups of 1 to 2 (rarely 3). Initially dormant, it awakens within 12 blocks and pursues up to 20 blocks before returning to rest.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.att: Danger level: high in narrow tunnels. Bears 36 HP (18 hearts), 6 mineral armor, heavy 0.22 movement speed and moderate knockback resistance (55%). Combines heavy melee strikes with ranged shard fire.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.com: Slag Slam: vertical strike dealing 5 HP after a 0.6 s wind-up. Tectonic Sweep: lateral frontal-arc swing dealing 4 HP after 0.8 s.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.tac: Amber Shard: channels mineral energy and fires a 4 HP projectile every 3 to 5 seconds, blocked by solid walls. After each heavy attack, the Lithophage enters recovery (0.6 to 0.9 s), opening a clear window to counter-attack.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.lithophage.spo: I: ancient clay. II: amber core.
Upon collapsing, it yields 12 experience, Ancient Clay Fragment (1 to 2, common) and, with a lower chance, a Mineral Amber Core.
item.codenamecoraline.last_gift_collecto: Nicolas Noel, the Renegade Spawn Egg
entity.codenamecoraline.last_gift_collec: The Collector of the Last Gift
The Silent Bell echoes across the frozen sky...
The Silent Bell must be rung upon Packed Ice.
The winter gale does not answer here. Seek a Snowy Taiga or Grove.
Nicolas Noel only crosses the sky at night.
The sky and clearing around the ice must be unobstructed.
Nicolas Noel already walks these snows.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.the: Nicolas Noel once brought the gifts. The villages stopped paying, and he came back as the Collector of the Last Gift. Defeat the Renegade and close the last debt of the solstice.
subtitles.codenamecoraline.entity.last_g: Nicolas Noel's sleigh cuts the sky
bestiary.codenamecoraline.last_gift_coll: Santa hat, long nose, great beard and greataxe.

A colossal 4.5-block fey in a burgundy coat trimmed with pale fur. A blue-grey face with a long, cold nose glares from under a Santa hat and a beard that reaches his belt. He carries a greataxe and a sack stitched with a skull.

Nicolas Noel once carried the gifts of the solstice, and every gift was a pledge. The villages stopped paying and he came back as the Collector of the Last Gift, with the same axe that cut his promise. Craft the Silent Bell (bell, 4 packed ice, soul lantern) and ring it at night on packed ice in a Snowy Taiga or Grove under open sky. The advancements tell the rest of his story.

420 HP, 10 armor (+4 toughness), 90% knockback resistance; he never freezes and powder snow does not hold him. Stages begin at 80, 60, 40, 20 and 10% health: 2 Gaze, Whirlwind and crescents; 3 comets, gift rain and Gift Mimics; 4 Frost Cone; 5 Frenzy (+4 damage); 6 RAGE: speed, armor and damage amplified.

His rhythm is never the same: wind-ups stretch and shrink, attacks chain into combos and he leads his shots. He answers kiting with comets and gift rain, and a pillar with magic. Look away from his Gaze, leave the gold-and-red rings before the presents land, and kill the Gift Mimics before they burst.
Overhead axe chop and a trailing comet.

Axe: cleave 11, overhead chop waves 7, whirlwind 6, crescent wave 9. Stomp 9, Solstice Leap 12. Magic: comets 8 (homing), gift rain 10, Frost Cone 8 with freezing, Gaze 5. Gift Mimics bite for 5 and burst for 7. Frenzy adds 4 to every hit; Rage multiplies by 1.5.
I: Greataxe. II: Cracked Bell. III: Thread. IV: Seal.

On his final collapse: 100 XP and the advancement The Final Delivery. A Christmas gift falls and pops open on a chest holding the Renegade's Greataxe (always), 1 Cracked Bell, 2 to 4 Frostbound Threads and a 20% chance for the rare Solstice Seal. His Gift Mimics vanish with him.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.sil: The Bell That Does Not Ring
They say the last gift of winter came with a bell that never sounds. Craft the Silent Bell: a bell, packed ice and a soul lantern.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.the: Every gift at the solstice was a pledge, and every pledge falls due. Ring the bell on packed ice, at night, in the snow, and Nicolas Noel will answer.
The Day the Sleigh Fell Silent
Nicolas's sleigh bell cracked the day the last village went quiet. Take the Cracked Bell from his gift.
Nicolas Noel cut his own promise with this axe, and called his gifts to heel with it. Now it is yours to carry.
Back when giving was an honour and not a debt, Nicolas sealed the first gift with this. Very few ever find it.
Nicolas Noel's axe. Right-click: call 3 Gift Mimics to fight for you.
Each call wears the axe (250 durability).
The axe is too worn to call more gifts.
Your Gift Mimics are still around.
subtitles.codenamecoraline.entity.canopy: The Canopy Breaker bellows in pain
Heavy footsteps of the Canopy Breaker
The Canopy Breaker flies into a fury
entity.codenamecoraline.canopy_breaker.s: The branches tremble. Something heavy is coming down from the canopy...
The idol must be set against a tree trunk.
Only the oldest forests answer: an old-growth taiga or a dark forest.
The beast only comes down at night.
There are too few old trees around to carry him.
There is no clearing near the trunk for him to land in.
The Canopy Breaker already rules this forest.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.canopy_breaker: Long arms, a bowed back and the Deadroot Club.

An ape-like beast of 3.1 blocks, with mossy bark-grey fur, arms longer than its legs and knuckles worn into hooks. On the move it runs on four limbs; to fight it draws a club of dead root from its back and stands. Its eyes glow amber in the dark of the canopy.

Loggers who cut the oldest trees said something up in the crown cut back. They carved hollow idols from dark oak, bone and moss to ask it to come down. Use the Hollow Trunk Idol on a log in an old-growth taiga or a dark forest, at night, with many trees around and a clearing nearby. A failed use never spends the idol and tells you what is missing.

200 HP, 8 armor, speed 0.33 on the ground, 3.1 blocks tall. Stage 1 guards the forest floor. At 60% health he becomes the Canopy Hunter and takes to the trees: climbing trunks, crossing between canopies in real jumps and dropping on you. At 25% he becomes the Fury of the Timber: faster, with shorter pauses. Each change happens once.

He never swings at empty air: watch the club. Step out of the circle before a Trunk Slam lands, leave the arc of a Canopy Sweep, and stay out of reach of the lunge when his shoulders drop. When he climbs, he is committed: you can break the trunk he is on or wait for the Canopy Drop marker on the ground and leave it. The Intimidating Roar does not take control from you.
Overhead slam and the mark on the ground.

Trunk Slam 7, Canopy Sweep 5, Brute Lunge 6, Backhand 4, Canopy Drop 8 (once per climb, only after a real descent). Every blow has a visible wind-up and a recovery window in which he can be staggered by a heavy hit.
I: Club. II: Resin. III: Heartwood.

On defeat, once: 60 XP, 2 to 4 Canopy Resin, 50% for a Heartwood Splinter and 30% for the Deadroot Club. The advancements Hollow Trunk, Something Answers, Felled Beast and Dead Root keep the rest of the story.
advancements.codenamecoraline.bosses.can: Loggers carved idols out of dark oak, bone and moss to call down what lives in the crowns. Craft a Hollow Trunk Idol.
Set the idol against a log in an old-growth taiga or a dark forest, at night, with many trees around. The canopy will answer.
Defeat the Canopy Breaker, whether on the forest floor, in the branches or in the air between the trees.
The beast carried a club of dead root on its back for longer than the forest has been standing. Take the Deadroot Club.
item.codenamecoraline.deadroot_club.lore: Hold right-click on the ground, release: the club pulls you where you look. Hold Shift in the air to dive and slam.
Shift + right-click calls Bark Macaques to fight beside you.
item.codenamecoraline.deadroot_club.airb: You must be on the ground to leap.
item.codenamecoraline.deadroot_club.too_: The club is too worn to call anyone.
item.codenamecoraline.deadroot_club.summ: Enough Bark Macaques already fight for you.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.baby_dragon.in: Some say these hatchlings come from warmth held deep within mountains. Four tiny paws, broad cheeks, membrane wings and a restless tail mark a dragon still small. Its red scales shelter a spark that never burns its own body.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.baby_dragon.ha: Search Overworld forests, taigas, groves and mountains. Uncommon, they appear alone or in pairs on solid ground with daylight and open sky. They have twenty health points and two armor; fire and falls cannot hurt them.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.baby_dragon.be: Wild hatchlings wander, watch travellers and make short flights. They do not hunt animals or seek fights. Give them room to spread their wings. A companion ordered to rest closes its eyes at night; feeding brings a happy wag of the tail.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.baby_dragon.ta: Offer raw salmon: each attempt consumes one and has a one-in-three chance of earning trust. Hearts confirm the bond. Afterwards only its owner may feed it, healing four points per salmon. Right-click with an empty hand to switch between resting and following.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.baby_dragon.co: It walks nearby, flies to keep up with running and makes irregular loops when you stop. Sneak and right-click it empty-handed to call it to your shoulder. After landing, release sneak, then hold it for one second to release the dragon. Water, vehicles, elytra flight, danger or combat also make it leave. Far away, it looks for safe ground near its owner.
bestiary.codenamecoraline.baby_dragon.de: The hatchling reacts to attacks and its owner’s fights. It charges for twelve ticks and fires an ember dealing three damage, with a 1.5-second cooldown before charging again. It never explodes or ignites scenery. Owner, allies and companions are spared. Sneak and right-click with a stick to toggle defense. The rest command takes priority.
